definition: Quality assurance is an organised system used in settings such as healthcare to monitor and improve how work is carried out, with the aim of supporting safe, consistent care. In this context, it refers to formal processes introduced during organisational change to maintain and evaluate standards.

reasons: The definition adds specific functions that are not supported by the packet, such as monitoring and improving how work is carried out, and maintaining and evaluating standards.

The packet supports a healthcare quality-assurance system and its implementation during organisational change, but it does not define quality assurance generally as the broader organised system described here.
The packet text does not provide a dictionary-like definition of “quality assurance” or specify that it is “an organised system…to monitor and improve how work is carried out.”

The packet mentions implementing a “quality assurance system” in a hospital and examines impact during organisational change/crisis, but it does not support the definition’s claim that it specifically “refers to formal processes introduced during organisational change to maintain and evaluate standards.”
